problem: Memory-persistent VLN methods either incorporate the entire accumulated memory (noisy, costly) or use fixed-horizon spatial lookup (loses valuable experience), and they store only environmental observations while ignoring navigation behavioral histories that encode decision strategies.
motivation: Agents that operate persistently should improve through accumulated experience, as humans do by imagining routes and consulting past experience. The paper uses imagination as a query mechanism: predicted future states are used to selectively retrieve relevant past observations and behaviors from explicit memory, which avoids hallucination and full-memory overhead.
key_idea: A language-conditioned contrastive world model imagines future latent states and uses them as queries to retrieve both observations and behavioral histories from a viewpoint-anchored hybrid memory, and a DUET-style navigation model fuses the retrieved knowledge.
insight: Retrieval quality is what matters: imagination-based retrieval beats full incorporation, random, instruction-similarity and state-similarity retrieval (IR2R val-unseen SPL 73.46 vs 69.98 for full, 72.82 for instruction, 72.85 for state). Instruction matching has high recall but poor precision because of temporal misalignment; state matching is path-dependent. Overshooting training, a Transformer backbone and world-model pretraining all help. The oracle retrieval upper bound (93.4 SPL) shows that world-model prediction quality is the main remaining bottleneck.
method: Language-conditioned contrastive RSSM world model: infers the latent state from the DUET viewpoint feature and instruction, imagines future states with a transition model, and predicts distance-to-goal to stop imagination (horizon D up to 5). It is trained with a reward term, an NCE state-observation compatibility term and a KL term, plus d-step overshooting.
Hybrid Viewpoint-Level Memory: an observation bank (viewpoint features) and a history bank (inferred states plus imagined trajectories per viewpoint), both anchored to a persistent topological graph.

Observation retrieval: for the i-th imagined state, score i-th-order neighbors in the persistent graph by cosine compatibility, apply a percentile filter (rho_o, gamma_o) and top-W selection, then add shortest paths (and neighbors) to the episodic graph.

History retrieval: match the imagined trajectory against stored imagined trajectories at the current viewpoint, with step-decayed thresholds. Rank by match length and minimum score, keep the top P patterns, and add the subsequent viewpoints and states to the graph.

Experience-augmented navigation model: extends DUET with a coarse encoder over retrieved nodes, a fine-scale encoder, and a navigation-history encoder that fuses softmax-weighted retrieved states with viewpoint features.
Dynamic fusion: the stop-token outputs of the three encoders are passed through an FFN and softmax to give weights that combine the three action score sets.
Training: joint pretraining of world model and navigator on R2R plus augmented trajectories, then imitation learning. The expert policy randomly samples among optimal paths.

setting.backbone: DUET / ScaleVLN / GR-DUET navigators with a Transformer or GRU RSSM world model (trained)
setting.training_data: R2R plus PREVALENT-augmented trajectories for pretraining (5,000 iterations, batch 32, lr 5e-5), then imitation learning on IR2R / GSA-R2R (lr 1e-5); ScaleVLN variant uses environment-augmented pretraining
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with topological graph
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (topological graph nodes plus stop)
setting.privileged: none (persistent memory accumulated from previous episodes; the connectivity graph is built online)

numbers_note: GSA-R2R is reported per scenario. Only 4 of the 10 scenarios appear in Table 2; the others (other user-instruction styles) are only in a radar figure. The split label 'test' is assumed for GSA-R2R (ablations call it 'Test-R-Basic'). IR2R is not in the canonical list, so it is labelled other:IR2R.
results: On IR2R val-unseen, Memoir on GR-DUET reaches SPL 73.3 and SR 77.6, versus 67.9 SPL for GR-DUET (+5.4), and it also lifts DUET (58.0→69.1 SPL) and ScaleVLN (66.5→72.1). On GSA-R2R it beats GR-DUET by about 2.3 SR and 2.5 SPL on average across the user-instruction scenarios and by 2.4 SR and 1.6 SPL across the eight scene/basic scenarios. It uses 8.3x faster training and 74% less inference memory than GR-DUET.
limitations: World-model prediction is imperfect (73.3 vs 93.4 SPL oracle), so retrieval is imprecise, can end imagination prematurely, and cannot separate spatially distinct targets.

Seen-environment performance of memory-persistent variants drops relative to the single-episode baseline, and the agent has no confidence estimate for retrieved memory or exploration/exploitation balance.
Inference latency is 28% higher than GR-DUET (0.31s vs 0.25s), driven by imagination. Evaluation is simulation-only.
